workflowDefinitions.name: FireAndForgetTaskWorkflow
workflowDefinitions.description: Lightweight fire-and-forget task delegation. Delegates a single task to the target agent — no result delivery, no notification. Designed for Temporal-scheduled tasks and one-off delegations where the result is visible in the dashboard but doesn't need to be reported back. Prefer TaskDelegationWorkflow when you need guaranteed result delivery to the CTO agent.

{{vars.review_response}}

workflowDefinitions.name: UweDesignWorkflow
workflowDefinitions.description: Creates or refines a well-specified GitHub issue with multi-agent consensus review, then gates on CEO design-approval. Consensus loop (max 3 rounds) — if exhausted or needs_human_review, escalates to CEO gate instead of cancelling. CEO wait loop (hourly reminders, no auto-cancel). Returns {IssueNumber: N} on approval. Replaces compiled DesignWorkflow. Epic grants (#436): the author outputs BODY_SHA256, consensus attests it (author and CTO excluded), it is published as ReviewRef only after a unanimous attested approval, the design gate is visit-guarded, and a grant decision re-hashes the issue body (verify_approved_body) and fails with ERROR:approved_artifact_changed on a mismatch. Human approvals skip the re-hash.

steps.name: create_or_refine
steps.instruction:
Your task is to create or refine a GitHub issue in repo {{input.Repo}}.

Determine which action to take by checking in priority order:
1. Prior issue number from previous iteration: {{vars.issue_result | extract: 'ISSUE_NUMBER:\s*(\d+)' | default: 'none'}} — if this is a number, REFINE that issue.
2. ExistingIssueNumber from input: {{input.ExistingIssueNumber | default: 'none'}} — if this is a number, REFINE that issue.
3. If neither is set — CREATE a new well-specified GitHub issue for: {{input.Description}}.

For CREATE: use `gh issue create --repo {{input.Repo}}`.
For REFINE: use `gh issue edit <N> --repo {{input.Repo}}`.

Incorporate this prior consensus feedback (if any):
{{vars.consensus_out.ConsolidatedReasoning | default: 'none'}}

Incorporate this prior CEO feedback (if any):
{{vars.approval_signal.Comment | default: 'none'}}

CEO consensus direction (if any):
{{vars.ceo_consensus_out.ConsolidatedReasoning | default: 'none'}}

At the end of your response, output exactly: ISSUE_NUMBER: <number>
After your last edit, also output the SHA-256 of the issue body bytes on its own line, computed with `gh issue view <number> --repo {{input.Repo}} --json body | jq -j .body | sha256sum` (first field):
BODY_SHA256: <64-hex>

When incorporating prior consensus or CEO feedback:
- Treat the comment as authoritative. Do not re-argue the design.
- Restate the concern in your own words in a comment on the issue/PR, so reviewers can verify you understood.
- Make the change the comment asks for. If you believe it is wrong, respond via changes_requested on the next round rather than ignoring it.

Every spec MUST include:
- A 'Files to Touch' section enumerating each file/path the implementer will modify.
- An 'Acceptance Criteria' section with testable assertions (not vague goals).
- A 'Constraints / MUST NOT' section listing at least 3 domain-specific dangers the implementation must avoid. Not generic boilerplate — concrete, workflow-specific MUST-NOTs.
- Every external dependency (DB, file, HTTP call, process) must have an explicit failure path stated.

args.Subject: Issue {{vars.issue_result | extract: 'ISSUE_NUMBER:\s*(\d+)'}} design spec in {{input.Repo}}
args.ReviewPrompt:
Review the design spec for GitHub issue {{vars.issue_result | extract: 'ISSUE_NUMBER:\s*(\d+)'}} in repo {{input.Repo}}. Fetch it with: gh issue view {{vars.issue_result | extract: 'ISSUE_NUMBER:\s*(\d+)'}} --repo {{input.Repo}}

Evaluate whether the spec is complete and unambiguous enough to implement without guessing. Check: are all edge cases covered? Are the code changes described precisely enough for an implementer to follow without design decisions of their own?

Review discipline:
- Fetch the current spec/PR fresh — do NOT summarize prior rounds.
- Verify each prior finding against the current text before reporting.
- Give structured findings with severity (blocker, high, medium, low).
- End your response with exactly one verdict line: VERDICT: approved | changes_requested | needs_human_review.

EVIDENCE MIRROR (best-effort, optional).
Post your full technical review as a comment on that GitHub issue/PR, then put the resulting comment URL on your EVIDENCE: line.
- Before posting, remove private identities, internal IDs, hostnames, workflow-run identifiers, and private incident or configuration details. The repository may be public. Your unsanitized response is retained in durable workflow history regardless.
- If the GitHub CLI, auth, API, or the comment post fails for any reason, write `EVIDENCE: none`, mention the mirror failure in one short clause in SUMMARY:, and still return every BLOCKER: line and your VERDICT:. A failed mirror never downgrades or fails the review — durable history is the source of truth, the comment is a convenience copy.
- If you are continuing a response that was cut off and the earlier part already contains an `EVIDENCE: https://...` URL, reuse that URL and do NOT post a second comment.

Issue body under review (ReviewRef): SHA-256 {{vars.body_sha | default: 'unknown'}}. Recompute it with `gh issue view {{vars.issue_result | extract: 'ISSUE_NUMBER:\s*(\d+)'}} --repo {{input.Repo}} --json body | jq -j .body | sha256sum` (first field) and request changes if it differs.

Reviewed-ref attestation (#436):
- End your review with `REVIEWED_REF: <ref>` for the ref you actually checked.
- If `{{input.Repo}}` is public, check that no private names, internal URLs, hosts, credentials or private links are present, and add `PUBLIC_SCRUB: pass` or `PUBLIC_SCRUB: fail`.

workflowDefinitions.name: UweDocMaintenanceWorkflow
workflowDefinitions.description: Post-merge documentation maintenance (#436): prepare (read-only artifact with ARTIFACT_SHA256), deterministic classify (only memory and repo_doc targets are delegable), consensus review of the exact artifact (PrepAgent and CTO excluded; skipped without ConsensusAgents), publish ReviewRef only after a unanimous attested approval of a delegable artifact, a visit-guarded doc-review gate, then apply exactly the approved artifact and check APPLIED_ARTIFACT_SHA256. Nothing is written before the gate. Max 2 rounds. Inputs: Repo, PrNumber, BranchName, MergeSummary, optional IssueNumber, ConsensusAgents and PrepAgent (empty → the CTO, which makes the gate human-only).

steps.name: prepare
steps.instruction:
Prepare the documentation changes for merged PR #{{input.PrNumber}} on branch `{{input.BranchName}}` in repo {{input.Repo}}.

This step READS ONLY. Do not write fleet-memory, project contexts, instructions, repository files, branches or PRs. Nothing is written before the doc-review gate; after approval exactly the artifact you return is applied.

Merge summary: {{input.MergeSummary}}

Gate feedback on the previous artifact (if any):
{{vars.doc_review | default: 'none'}}

Review feedback on the previous artifact (if any):
{{vars.doc_consensus_out.ConsolidatedReasoning | default: 'none'}}

Steps:
1. Fetch the diff: `gh pr diff {{input.PrNumber}} --repo {{input.Repo}}`
2. Decide whether any documentation must change: architecture, config, ports, services, schemas, tool mappings, docker config, CI/CD or infrastructure, as described in fleet-memory entries (including 'WorkflowType — operational context' memories), repository docs, project contexts or agent instructions.
3. If nothing must change, output exactly the line: PREP: NO_DOC
4. Otherwise output, in this order:
PREP: ARTIFACT
TARGET: <type> <id>   (one line per target; type is memory, repo_doc, project_context or instruction; id is the memory id or 'new', owner/repo:path, the context name or the instruction name)
ARTIFACT_SHA256: <64-hex>
-----BEGIN DOC ARTIFACT-----
<the complete new content for every target, each section headed by its TARGET line>
-----END DOC ARTIFACT-----

The artifact hash is the SHA-256 of the artifact body: every line strictly between the two marker lines, each terminated by a single LF, UTF-8. Compute it with:
awk '/^-----BEGIN DOC ARTIFACT-----$/{f=1;next}/^-----END DOC ARTIFACT-----$/{f=0}f' <file> | sha256sum

steps.name: notify_prepare_invalid
steps.instruction: Post to the Telegram group: doc maintenance for PR #{{input.PrNumber}} in {{input.Repo}} stopped: the prepare step returned neither PREP: NO_DOC nor PREP: ARTIFACT. Nothing was written.

args.Subject: Documentation artifact for PR #{{input.PrNumber}} in {{input.Repo}}
args.ReviewPrompt:
Review the documentation artifact prepared for merged PR #{{input.PrNumber}} in repo {{input.Repo}}. Nothing has been written yet; after approval exactly this artifact is applied.

Prepared output (the artifact is between the marker lines):
{{vars.prep_result}}

Check it against the PR diff (`gh pr diff {{input.PrNumber}} --repo {{input.Repo}}`): accurate, complete, and limited to documentation.

Artifact under review (ReviewRef): ARTIFACT_SHA256 {{vars.artifact_sha | default: 'unknown'}}. Recompute it from the artifact text and request changes if it differs. The artifact hash is the SHA-256 of the artifact body: every line strictly between the two marker lines, each terminated by a single LF, UTF-8. Compute it with:
awk '/^-----BEGIN DOC ARTIFACT-----$/{f=1;next}/^-----END DOC ARTIFACT-----$/{f=0}f' <file> | sha256sum

Review discipline:
- Give structured findings with severity (blocker, high, medium, low).
- End your response with exactly one verdict line: VERDICT: approved | changes_requested | needs_human_review.

Reviewed-ref attestation (#436):
- End your review with `REVIEWED_REF: <ref>` for the ref you actually checked.
- If `{{input.Repo}}` is public, check that no private names, internal URLs, hosts, credentials or private links are present, and add `PUBLIC_SCRUB: pass` or `PUBLIC_SCRUB: fail`.

notifyStep.name: notify_doc_review
notifyStep.instruction:
Post to the Telegram group:

Documentation artifact ready for PR #{{input.PrNumber}} in {{input.Repo}}. Nothing has been written yet.

Prepared output:
{{vars.prep_result}}

Review: {{vars.doc_consensus_out.FinalVerdict | default: 'not run'}}
{{vars.doc_consensus_out.ConsolidatedReasoning | default: ''}}
Delegable (memory and repo_doc targets only): {{vars.delegable}}

Decision impact:
- approved: exactly this artifact is applied
- changes_requested: a new artifact is prepared and reviewed (2 rounds in total)
- rejected: nothing is applied, and there is nothing to clean up

Please review and signal the workflow with 'doc-review':
  {"Decision":"approved"} — apply the artifact
  {"Decision":"changes_requested","Comment":"your feedback"} — prepare a new artifact
  {"Decision":"rejected","Comment":"reason"} — apply nothing

Epic grant (#436): gate visit `{{vars.doc_visit}}`, reviewed ref `{{vars.review_ref | default: 'none'}}`. With no reviewed ref this gate is a human decision only. Under an active epic grant the configured CTO agent may approve this exact visit after an independent review with {"Decision":"approved","GrantId":"<grant id>","VisitId":"<this visit>","ArtifactRef":"<reviewed ref>","Evidence":"<https url>"}; the orchestrator checks the grant and sends it, and the workflow discards any approval naming another visit or ref.

steps.name: apply
steps.instruction:
The doc-review gate approved the documentation artifact for PR #{{input.PrNumber}} in {{input.Repo}}. Apply EXACTLY the artifact below — nothing else and no extra edits.

Prepared output (the artifact is between the marker lines):
{{vars.prep_result}}

For each TARGET:
- memory: memory_store / memory_update with exactly the artifact content.
- repo_doc: open a PR with exactly the artifact content for that path, then merge it (squash).
- project_context: update_project_context with exactly the artifact content.
- instruction: update_instruction with exactly the artifact content, then reprovision_agent for each agent that uses it.

Then recompute the hash of the artifact you applied. The artifact hash is the SHA-256 of the artifact body: every line strictly between the two marker lines, each terminated by a single LF, UTF-8. Compute it with:
awk '/^-----BEGIN DOC ARTIFACT-----$/{f=1;next}/^-----END DOC ARTIFACT-----$/{f=0}f' <file> | sha256sum

Output exactly one line with it:
APPLIED_ARTIFACT_SHA256: <64-hex>

steps.name: notify_apply_mismatch
steps.instruction: Post to the Telegram group: doc maintenance for PR #{{input.PrNumber}} in {{input.Repo}} FAILED its apply check. The applied artifact hash ({{vars.applied_sha | default: 'missing'}}) does not match the approved artifact ({{vars.expected_sha | default: 'missing'}}). Check what was written; no retry was made.

workflowDefinitions.name: UwePrImplementationWorkflow
workflowDefinitions.description: Implements a GitHub issue on a branch, opens PR, runs consensus review loop (max 5 rounds), CEO merge-approval gate (max 5 rounds with changes_requested loop), merges, and fires DocMaintenanceWorkflow. Replaces compiled PrImplementationWorkflow. Epic grants (#436): the reviewed PR head is pinned (HEAD_SHA → consensus ReviewRef, author and CTO excluded), published as ReviewRef only after a unanimous attested approval, the merge gate is visit-guarded, a grant decision merges with --match-head-commit, and doc maintenance receives IssueNumber, ConsensusAgents and PrepAgent (optional input DocPrepAgent).

steps.name: phase1_implement
steps.instruction:
Before acting, honor the memory hint that will be appended to this message — search fleet-memory for operational context keyed to this workflow type.

Implement the following task in repo {{input.Repo}}. When done, open a PR against main.

Task:
  Issue number: {{input.IssueNumber | default: 'N/A'}}
  Description: {{input.Description | default: 'none'}}

Branch name: Use `{{input.BranchName}}` if it is provided and non-empty. Otherwise, auto-generate: use `feat/issue-{{input.IssueNumber}}` if an issue number is provided, or a short `feat/<description-slug>` for description-only tasks.

At the end of your response, output the PR URL on its own line:

PR head under review (ReviewRef): {{vars.head_sha | default: 'unknown'}}. Run `gh pr view {{vars.pr_url}} --repo {{input.Repo}} --json headRefOid` and request changes if the head differs from it.

Reviewed-ref attestation (#436):

notifyStep.instruction:

steps.name: phase2_5_unresolved_check
steps.instruction:
Before acting, honor the memory hint that will be appended to this message — search fleet-memory for operational context keyed to this workflow type.

Check the PR at {{vars.pr_url}} in repo {{input.Repo}} for any unresolved review comments (use `gh pr view --json reviews,reviewRequests` and `gh api repos/{{input.Repo}}/pulls` to inspect). If there are unresolved inline comments or review threads, address each one — push any fixes to the branch. If there are none, confirm all review comments have been addressed. Report: either 'no unresolved comments' or a summary of what was fixed.

notifyStep.instruction:
Post to Telegram group: PR for issue #{{input.IssueNumber | default: 'N/A'}} in repo {{input.Repo}} ({{vars.pr_url}}) has been approved by consensus and is ready to merge.

Context for your decision:
- PR: {{vars.pr_url}}
- Consensus: reviewers approved the implementation as correct and complete
- Consensus reasoning: {{vars.consensus_out.ConsolidatedReasoning | default: 'see PR review'}}
- approved → PR is merged immediately and doc maintenance runs; changes_requested → re-enters consensus review loop; rejected → PR is closed without merging

Send the 'merge-approval' signal to this workflow:
  {"Decision":"approved"} — approve and merge
  {"Decision":"changes_requested","Comment":"feedback"} — request changes before merging
  {"Decision":"rejected","Comment":"reason"} — reject and close without merging

Epic grant (#436): gate visit `{{vars.merge_visit}}`, reviewed ref `{{vars.review_ref | default: 'none'}}`. With no reviewed ref this gate is a human decision only. Under an active epic grant the configured CTO agent may approve this exact visit after an independent review with {"Decision":"approved","GrantId":"<grant id>","VisitId":"<this visit>","ArtifactRef":"<reviewed ref>","Evidence":"<https url>"}; the orchestrator checks the grant and sends it, and the workflow discards any approval naming another visit or ref.

steps.name: notify_merge_timeout
steps.instruction: Post to Telegram group: PrImplementationWorkflow for issue #{{input.IssueNumber | default: 'N/A'}} in {{input.Repo}} auto-cancelled: no merge-approval response after 3 hours.

steps.name: notify_merge_rejected
steps.instruction: Post to Telegram group: PR for issue #{{input.IssueNumber | default: 'N/A'}} in {{input.Repo}} ({{vars.pr_url}}) rejected by CEO at merge gate. Reason: {{vars.merge_decision.Comment | default: 'no reason given'}}

args.Subject: CEO merge-gate feedback on PR for issue #{{input.IssueNumber | default: 'N/A'}} in {{input.Repo}}
args.ReviewPrompt:
Review the PR at {{vars.pr_url}} in repo {{input.Repo}}.

The CEO has reviewed the approved PR and requested changes before merging:
{{vars.merge_decision.Comment | default: 'no specific comment'}}

Evaluate whether the CEO's concerns are valid and warrant code changes.
Implementation summary:
{{vars.impl_result}}

Prior review history:
{{vars.consensus_out.ConsolidatedReasoning | default: 'none'}}

Review discipline:
- Fetch the current spec/PR fresh — do NOT summarize prior rounds.
- Verify each prior finding against the current text before reporting.
- Give structured findings with severity (blocker, high, medium, low).
- End your response with exactly one verdict line: VERDICT: approved | changes_requested | needs_human_review.

EVIDENCE MIRROR (best-effort, optional).
Post your full technical review as a comment on that GitHub issue/PR, then put the resulting comment URL on your EVIDENCE: line.
- Before posting, remove private identities, internal IDs, hostnames, workflow-run identifiers, and private incident or configuration details. The repository may be public. Your unsanitized response is retained in durable workflow history regardless.
- If the GitHub CLI, auth, API, or the comment post fails for any reason, write `EVIDENCE: none`, mention the mirror failure in one short clause in SUMMARY:, and still return every BLOCKER: line and your VERDICT:. A failed mirror never downgrades or fails the review — durable history is the source of truth, the comment is a convenience copy.
- If you are continuing a response that was cut off and the earlier part already contains an `EVIDENCE: https://...` URL, reuse that URL and do NOT post a second comment.

changes_requested.name: revise_ceo_feedback
changes_requested.instruction:
Before acting, honor the memory hint that will be appended to this message — search fleet-memory for operational context keyed to this workflow type.

The CEO requested changes before merging the PR in repo {{input.Repo}}.

CEO feedback: {{vars.merge_decision.Comment | default: 'no specific comment'}}

Reviewers have confirmed the CEO's concerns are valid. Apply the necessary changes and push to the branch.

Reviewer consensus on CEO feedback:
{{vars.ceo_consensus_out.ConsolidatedReasoning}}

Prior feedback:
{{vars.consensus_out.ConsolidatedReasoning | default: 'none'}}

When incorporating prior consensus or CEO feedback:
- Treat the comment as authoritative. Do not re-argue the design.
- Restate the concern in your own words in a comment on the issue/PR, so reviewers can verify you understood.
- Make the change the comment asks for. If you believe it is wrong, respond via changes_requested on the next round rather than ignoring it.

At the end of your response, output the PR head commit after your push, on its own line (from `gh pr view {{vars.pr_url}} --repo {{input.Repo}} --json headRefOid`):
HEAD_SHA: <40-hex commit sha>
